question_text: A small, uniaxial stress of $1 \mathrm{MPa}(145 \mathrm{psi})$ is applied to a rod of high-density polyethylene. (a) Given $E=830 \mathrm{MPa}$, what is the resulting strain? (b) Given $E=1.3 \mathrm{MPa}$, repeat for a rod of vulcanized isoprene. (c) Given $E=2 \times 10^5 \mathrm{MPa}$, repeat for a rod of 1040 steel. Give your answer as a tuple (strain for polyethylene, strain for isoprene, strain for steel).
response:
For a uniaxial elastic stress, $\varepsilon = \sigma/E$.

**(a) High-density polyethylene:**
$$\varepsilon = \frac{1\ \text{MPa}}{830\ \text{MPa}} = \frac{1}{830} \approx 1.20\times10^{-3}$$

**(b) Vulcanized isoprene:**
$$\varepsilon = \frac{1\ \text{MPa}}{1.3\ \text{MPa}} = \frac{1}{1.3} \approx 0.769$$

**(c) 1040 steel:**
$$\varepsilon = \frac{1\ \text{MPa}}{2\times10^{5}\ \text{MPa}} = 5\times10^{-6}$$

The steel is ~$10^5$ times stiffer than the rubber, so its strain is correspondingly ~$10^5$ times smaller.

$$\boxed{\left(1.20\times10^{-3},\ 0.769,\ 5\times10^{-6}\right)}$$
